# Lab 5.3: Python UDFs

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a Python UDF that uses a PyPI package to clean text, and call it from SQL.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create the Python UDF.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION lab05.clean_text(x STRING)
RETURNS STRING
LANGUAGE python
OPTIONS (
  entry_point = 'clean',
  runtime_version = 'python-3.11',
  packages = ['unidecode']
)
AS r'''
from unidecode import unidecode

def clean(x):
    if x is None:
        return None
    return " ".join(unidecode(x).lower().split())
''';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT lab05.clean_text('  Café   CRÈME   Brûlée ') AS cleaned;</span>

5. **[Console] Check the cost.** Open **Job information**. Python UDFs use extra compute for the Python containers, billed under BigQuery services. Keep inputs small while testing.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Language | `python`, persistent functions only |
| Packages | Installed from PyPI |
| Output | Accents removed, spaces cleaned |
| Cost | Extra Python compute on top of the query |
